```{r}
rating_data <- read.csv("Arena_raw_2026-09-25.csv")
price_data <- read.csv("OpenRouter_raw_2026-09-28.csv")
rating_data %>% count(category, sort=TRUE)
```
```{r}
namecleaner <- function(x) {
  x %>%
    str_to_lower() %>%
    str_remove("^[^/]+/") %>%
   # str_remove(":batch$") %>%
    str_replace_all("[^a-z0-9]", "")
}
rating_data <- mutate(rating_data, modelname = namecleaner(model_name))
price_data <- mutate(price_data,modelname = namecleaner(id), is_batch = str_ends(id, ":batch"))
```
Batch models may not be included when doing actual modeling. 
```{r}
overall_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "overall")
english_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "overall")
non_english_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "non_english")
math_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "math")
coding_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "coding")
lit_ratings <- rating_data %>% filter(category == "creative_writing") 
```
I split each rating category into its own dataframe, but if it becomes necessary in the future they can be joined by model name if need be.

```{r}
sum(is.na(overall_ratings))
sum(is.na(price_data))
```
There are a great deal of columns in price_data that have a bunch of empty entries.
I got rid of all columns that aren't pricing that contain more than 25% empty values, and then found some remaining
columns which I did not consider useful for analysis, so I removed them as well. 
```{r}
junkcols <- c("canonical_slug", "hugging_face_id", "supported_parameters", 
                    "default_parameters", "supported_voices", "knowledge_cutoff", 
                    "expiration_date", "links.details", "benchmarks.design_arena", "pricing.overrides",
              "alias_target.name", "alias_target.slug","original_json")
price_red <- price_data[, colMeans(is.na(price_data)) <= 0.25 | grepl("^pricing", names(price_data))] %>% select(-all_of(junkcols))
price_red
```

```{r}
merged <- price_red %>%
  inner_join(overall_ratings, by = "modelname")
```
